finding.claim: Broken authorization: wipe() calls requireRole(), which returns a boolean and never throws, and ignores the result. Any authenticated user can therefore wipe any tenant without the OWNER role. The sibling export() uses checkRole(), which does throw, so the check is enforced there.
finding.source: Any authenticated caller of POST /tenants/{t}/wipe, with an arbitrary User whose roles lack OWNER and an attacker-chosen tenant path parameter.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant), a destructive deletion of the tenant's data.

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) is the handler for the endpoint; both arguments come from the request.
requireRole() only returns u.roles().contains(role) and its javadoc says it does not throw.
The boolean return value is discarded, so the check has no effect.

finding.guards_checked: Looked for any other role or ownership check in wipe() and found none. The only file in the repo is Admin.java, so I could not see upstream middleware. checkRole() is correctly used in export() at line 32, which confirms the intended behavior and shows that wipe() is the one that is broken.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole() at Admin.java:14 only returns a boolean and never throws, and the result is discarded at line 26. checkRole() at line 18 throws, but only export() calls it (line 32). No other guard exists in the repo; upstream middleware cannot be seen.
verdict.reason: Admin.java:26 calls requireRole(), which returns a boolean (Admin.java:14-16) and does not throw. It discards the result, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any caller. export() uses the throwing checkRole() at line 32.
